instructions: Sprinkle the yeast over 1/4 cup lukewarm water (105 to 115°F/40 to 46°C), stir, and leave it for 10 minutes, until frothy.

Warm the milk until it's just warm to the touch. Melt 4 tbsp of the butter and let it cool a little. In a large bowl or a stand mixer, mix the egg, honey, coriander, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, salt, warm milk, melted butter and 1 cup of the flour.
Add the yeast mixture and mix well. Add the rest of the flour 1/2 cup at a time, until you have a soft dough.
Knead on a lightly floured counter for 5 minutes, using as little extra flour as you can, until smooth and stretchy.
Put the dough in an oiled bowl and turn it once to coat. Cover and leave it in a warm spot for 1 to 2 hours, until doubled.
Grease a 3-quart round baking dish (3 inches deep) or a 10-inch springform pan generously with the remaining 2 tbsp butter.
Punch the dough down, knead it briefly and shape it into a ball. Press it into the pan so it covers the bottom. Cover and leave it for about 1 hour, until it reaches the rim of the pan.
Near the end of the rise, heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Bake for about 1 hour, until the top is golden brown. If you have a thermometer, the center should be 190°F (88°C). No thermometer? Tap the bottom of the loaf. It should sound hollow.
Let the loaf sit in the pan for 5 minutes, then move it to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. Slice and serve.
To keep it for the week, freeze the slices in a single layer on a baking sheet, then move them to a freezer bag. Warm a few slices in the oven when you want them.
method_notes: Tara's Multicultural Table leads: a milk, honey and egg dough with coriander, cinnamon, cloves and ginger, baked low at 300°F for about an hour. My Cooking Journey uses a smaller dough baked at 325°F for 35 to 40 minutes, and Cozy Delicious a milk-free honey and water dough with cardamom and nutmeg baked at 350°F. None shows a rating, so this counts as a fallback. Tara's page itself says the coriander may really be cardamom; coriander is kept here. Plan on about 3 hours of rising on top of the 30 minutes of prep and the hour in the oven. Best the day it's baked; freezing the slices is from Tara's.
